title: Copilot in Planning Parameter Worksheet
summary: A custom extension called Planning Parameter Worksheet uses Copilot powered by Azure OpenAI to suggest inventory planning parameters for items based on ABC classification and usage data. The AI evaluates one item at a time, applies established economic formulas, and explains its parameter recommendations.

title: Business Central Configuration Audit using Vibe Coding
summary: A consultant created a Business Central configuration audit extension using AI-assisted vibe coding to check for 200+ data issues like circular BOMs, missing posting groups, and incomplete setups. The AI agent generated over 5400 lines of code in basic structures, requiring minimal manual adjustments and making the project feasible where writing it manually would have been impractical.

title: Quality Management in Business Central Version 28
summary: Business Central version 28 adds a native Quality Management module for inspecting goods at purchase receipt, production output, assembly output, sales returns and in ad-hoc or scheduled checks. Templates, generation rules, inspection records, result-based usage blocking and quarantine workflows are covered. The extension was not installed automatically on upgrade and had to be added from AppSource.

title: ERP JumpStart: A Better Way to Get Started with Business Central
summary: ERP JumpStart is a guided self-service implementation product for smaller companies transitioning to Business Central. It combines pre-configuration, step-by-step tasks grouped in work packages, and integrated learning content to enable companies to set up and learn the system at their own pace without complex traditional ERP methodology.

title: Approval Workflows in Planning Worksheet
summary: Business Central version 28 adds approval workflow support to planning, requisition, and subcontracting worksheets at the batch level, allowing managers to review and approve suggested actions before they become real purchase orders or production orders. This feature prevents costly mistakes when planners carry out planning suggestions and addresses compliance requirements for segregation of duties.

title: Allow Posting Date Formula
summary: Business Central now supports date formulas for allowed posting dates in General Ledger Setup and User Setup, eliminating the common first-of-month panic when users cannot post transactions outside their allowed date range. This feature allows flexible, formula-based date restrictions that adjust automatically based on the current date.

title: How User and AI Agent Avatars Improve Record Ownership in Business Central BC 28
summary: Business Central BC 28 adds visual avatars for record creators and modifiers on list pages, showing who created or last changed a record without opening the full card. This helps teams identify ownership, reduce duplicate work, and distinguish human-created from AI-generated records.

title: How to Add Currency Symbols to Numeric Fields in Business Central.
summary: BC28 introduces configurable currency symbols on numeric fields to help finance users quickly identify whether transaction amounts are in local or foreign currency. Administrators can choose symbol position and display type globally or per currency without requiring custom development.

title: AI-Part1: what-is-GitHub-copilot-in-vscode-business-central.
summary: GitHub Copilot in VS Code evolved from simple autocomplete to a spectrum of capabilities including inline suggestions, chat, agent mode, and cloud agents. For Business Central AL developers, understanding these distinct modes and their constraints is essential because generic tutorials for other languages don't account for BC-specific patterns like event subscribers, table extensions, and object ID ranges.

title: New ModuleInfo Properties in Business Central 29
summary: Business Central 29 adds four new ModuleInfo properties (Help, EULA, PrivacyStatement, ContextSensitiveHelpUrl) that let AL developers retrieve application manifest metadata programmatically. These properties require runtime 18.0 or later and help extensions avoid duplicating configuration URLs in code.

title: Untangling Your Books: Understanding Application of Entries in Business Central
summary: Application of entries is the process of matching transactions like invoices and payments in Business Central to maintain accurate financial records. The post explains what open entries are, why matching is critical for accounting accuracy, and describes two main application methods: manual application and applying during payment posting.

title: How to Use the Copy Location Feature in Business Central 2026 Wave 1 (BC28)
summary: The Copy Location feature in Business Central BC28 allows users to duplicate existing warehouse and location configurations instead of setting them up manually, reducing implementation time and standardizing setups across multiple locations.

title: How Business Central 2026 Improves Item Variant Management with Pictures and Attributes.
summary: Business Central 2026 adds pictures and variant-level attributes to item variants, enabling faster product identification and more accurate product information management. This helps organizations with multiple product variations reduce errors and maintain better inventory data.

title: How to Migrate Business Central Table Fields from Integer to BigInteger.
summary: Business Central version 29 enables developers to migrate table fields from Integer to BigInteger without data loss during upgrades when targeting runtime 18.0 or later. This addresses scenarios where record identifiers exceed the 32-bit integer limit, while requiring careful handling of dependent code that may face narrowing conversions.

title: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2: Turn SIFT Indexes On or Off
summary: Starting with Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2, administrators can now turn SIFT (SumIndexField Technology) indexes on or off directly in the application through Table Information. This feature provides operational control over database performance by allowing targeted index management based on actual usage patterns without requiring developer changes or application modifications.

title: How to Email Posted Sales Shipments and Return Receipts in Business Central 2026 Wave 1.
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 adds email delivery, PDF generation, and attachment management for Posted Sales Shipments and Posted Return Receipts, enabling organizations to send shipment confirmations and return documentation directly from the system instead of relying on manual exports and external email.

title: Manage Database Index Usage in Business Central.
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 enables administrators to manage database indexes directly from the client without SQL access. The feature allows viewing index metrics, disabling unused secondary indexes per company, and optimizing database storage and write performance.

title: How to Export CSV Files from Business Central Using CSV Buffer (Developer Guide)
summary: This guide explains how to export data from Business Central to CSV format using the CSV Buffer table, covering its structure, recommended architecture, common export issues, and performance best practices for developers building integration and data exchange solutions.

title: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2 Preview Is Now Available
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 (version 29.0) preview is now available for testing by customers, partners, developers, and consultants to validate solutions and report issues before production rollout.

title: AI-Part2: Setup-Vscode-al-copilot-business-central
summary: Setting up Visual Studio Code, the AL Language extension, and GitHub Copilot for Business Central AL development requires installation of three components and verification of connections. This post guides developers through each setup step and highlights common gotchas like extension version mismatches and separate subscription management.

title: How to Use Date Formulas for Allowed Posting Periods in Business Central BC28.
summary: Business Central BC28 introduces dynamic date formulas for allowed posting periods that automatically calculate posting windows based on the current date instead of requiring manual updates. Administrators can configure these formulas in General Ledger Setup, User Setup, and Journal Templates to automate posting restrictions and reduce monthly maintenance.

title: Business Central 29.0 Is Generally Available: What Cloud Customers and Partners Need to Do.
summary: Business Central version 29.0 (2026 release wave 2) is now generally available, marking the start of the next upgrade cycle for cloud customers. New customers will be provisioned with version 29.0, and existing Business Central 28 customers should prepare for upgrades through testing, notification configuration, extension validation, and scheduled maintenance planning.

title: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 1 Installation Guide: Requirements, Prerequisites, and Setup Walkthrough
summary: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 1 (BC28) installation requires Windows 11 or Windows Server 2022/2025, .NET 8, SQL Server compatibility level 160/170, and 16 GB RAM minimum. This guide details system prerequisites, hardware requirements, software components, and a step-by-step installation process to help consultants and administrators avoid common deployment issues.

title: Business Central 29.0: Major Change to Table Extensions and SQL Storage.
summary: Business Central 29.0 changes how table extension fields are stored in the database, moving from a companion-table model to storing extension fields directly in the same SQL table as the base table. This enables cross-table indexes, can improve query performance, and requires developers to avoid direct SQL dependencies.

title: Automating Posting Periods in Business Central with Date Formulas
summary: Date formulas enable automatic posting period adjustments in Business Central based on today's date instead of fixed dates. This feature applies to General Ledger Setup, User Setup, and General Journal Templates, reducing manual updates and posting errors.

title: Preview Images Directly in the Business Central Web Client
summary: Business Central now supports previewing image attachments directly in the web client without downloading. The feature works with multiple image formats across attachments, agents, email, and FactBox thumbnails, with developers using File.ViewFromStream (online) or File.View (on-premises) to integrate the functionality into extensions.

title: Why No. Series Break After Upgrading to Business Central 27 (And How to Fix It)
summary: Business Central 27 enforces stricter Number Series validation during record insert, breaking master records that worked in BC 26 due to deferred validation. The fix involves auditing master entities, validating setup tables, and ensuring Number Series assignment before insert.

title: 🚀 Exploring Vibe Coding with GitHub Copilot for Business Central.
summary: Vibe Coding is a development approach where developers partner with AI tools like GitHub Copilot to co-create AL solutions for Business Central by providing context through coding standards, requirement documents, and integration with Microsoft Learn MCP. The post explains practical setup steps and how to configure Copilot Agent mode for holistic project development.

title: How to Group and Consolidate General Journal Lines Using Query Object in Business Central.
summary: This post explains how to consolidate General Journal Lines in Business Central using Query Objects to group records by Posting Date, Account No., and Dimension Set ID, then aggregate amounts and insert consolidated results into a target journal batch. It addresses a common developer scenario where multiple journal lines with identical keys need to be combined.

title: Directions Asia 2026 Recap: Key Takeaways from Ho Chi Minh City
summary: Directions Asia 2026 in Ho Chi Minh City focused on AI's transformation of Business Central from a system of record to a system of action, with live demonstrations of autonomous agents for accounts payable, sales orders, and expenses. The conference highlighted emerging partner competencies in agent design, integration architecture evolution, and governance frameworks needed for AI-driven implementations.

title: Evolve AL Interfaces with Default Implementations in Business Central 29.0
summary: Business Central 29.0 introduces default method implementations for AL interfaces, allowing interface contracts to evolve without immediately breaking existing implementations. The feature works with RequiredPending and analyzer rules to create a staged migration path where interface authors can add new methods with fallback behavior and gradually require explicit implementations over time.

title: Business Central ToolTip and ToolTipML Properties Are Now Available on Pages
summary: Business Central now supports ToolTip and ToolTipML properties directly on page objects, allowing navigation actions to inherit tooltips from their target pages rather than requiring duplicate tooltip definitions on each action.

title: Business Central Version 29: Recently Searched in Tell Me and Recently Used Lookups
summary: Business Central Version 29 introduces Recently Searched in Tell Me and Recently Used Lookups to help users navigate faster and enter data more efficiently. These personalized features reduce repetitive searching and clicks by surfacing frequently accessed pages and records based on user behavior patterns.

title: AL Development with Claude Code: A Multi-Agent Workflow
summary: AL development with Claude Code works best using a multi-agent workflow where specialized agents handle planning, development, code review, testing, and diagnostics sequentially. This approach keeps context manageable by writing results to files and reading only relevant documents, enabling extended development cycles and consistent output quality.

title: AL Language Tests: An Executable Spec for How BC Actually Behaves
summary: The BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests repository creates an executable specification of AL language behavior by running tests against real BC service tiers across multiple versions. It ensures AL Runner (an AL emulator) behaves accurately and provides a reference for undocumented AL features verified by CI.

title: AL Runner: A Weekend of Autonomous Agents, a Windows Cross-Check, and 59% of Microsoft's Tests Passing
summary: Stefan Maron describes a weekend of autonomous agent loops on AL Runner, shipped as v2.11.0, and its companion AL language test suite, which grew by 832 tests. A new nightly Windows workflow found a missing TestPermissions property in about 100 test codeunits and 8 behavioral differences between BC on Linux and real BC. A full run of Microsoft's BaseApp tests now passes 59.2%, and a hang was traced to a dropped report MaxIteration property.

title: AL Runner v2.2 and v2.3: Coverage, Quick Scripts, and a Watch Mode You Can Trust
summary: AL Runner v2.2 and v2.3 added code coverage reporting, a quick-script execute command for testing snippets without a codeunit, and fixed a watch mode that was recompiling mid-save during file bursts. The releases also included roughly 130 behavioral fixes to align the runner with real Business Central, with startup performance improvements.

title: AL Runner: Run AL Unit Tests Without a BC Service Tier
summary: AL Runner is a CLI tool that transpiles AL code to C# and executes unit tests in-memory without a BC service tier, Docker, or SQL Server, completing test runs in seconds instead of 20-30 minutes. It uses the BC compiler's public API to convert AL objects to C#, rewrites runtime types with mocks, and compiles everything with Roslyn for fast local testing.

title: AL Runner: Testing Against Real Cronus Data, Debugging Restored, and Mutation-Ready Coverage
summary: AL Runner, an in-memory test runner for Business Central AL code, gained several capabilities through v2.10.0: a --test-data flag that loads real Cronus demo rows from the BC backup, restored breakpoint debugging via a Debug Adapter Protocol server, per-test coverage for mutation testing, and TDD mode that now works with watch. v2.8.0 also makes compilation fail whenever the BC compiler reports an error.

title: AL Runner v2: What Feedback Told Me v1 Was Missing
summary: AL Runner v2 introduces a fundamental architecture change that enables integration testing against real Microsoft and third-party dependencies instead of mocks, moving from type-renaming and stubbing to using BC's own compiler and patching only low-level database operations. The update emphasizes fail-loudly error handling so tests cannot silently pass with wrong results, and introduces a separate language behavior test suite that validates all tests against real Business Central before trusting them.

title: If You Can't Make It Fast, Make It Feel Fast
summary: When operations take time despite optimization, BC developers can make them feel faster by moving blocking work to the background instead of waiting for user input. The post explores four background processing tools (Page Background Tasks, StartSession, TaskScheduler, and Job Queue), their use cases, and how BC online's auto-scaling distributes batch workloads across server instances to keep UI sessions responsive.

title: Introducing bc-code-atlas: Real BC Source for Coding Agents, Not a Guess
summary: bc-code-atlas is an MCP server, with a hosted instance and a self-host option, that lets AI agents or humans search Business Central Base Application source across versions and country variants. It combines semantic search, an exact call/subscribe/extend graph built on graphify-al, exact-source lookup tools, and version and country diffing so every hit can be checked against the real AL file. The author notes it is young: the public instance has no real authentication and has had outages.

title: BC on Linux: A Working Web Client, Faster Boots, Local Dev on Mac and Linux, and a Fast Lane in AL-Go
summary: Running Business Central on Linux now supports a working web client for local development, achieving cold boot times of 79 seconds and test runs of 1,067 tests in 69 seconds. The project includes AL-Go integration with a Linux fast lane for pull requests and snapshot-based caching for even faster development cycles.

title: Introducing bcdb: Read a Business Central Backup Without SQL Server
summary: bcdb is a tool that reads SQL Server backup files (.bak) and Business Central cloud exports (.bacpac) directly without requiring SQL Server or a restore process. It decodes table data using AL field names when provided with extension symbols and supports library and CLI usage.

title: bcdb restore: Write a Cloud Export Into a Container
summary: The bcdb restore tool writes cloud exports directly into a running Docker container without requiring matching schemas, intelligently handling mismatches by skipping missing tables and columns. It restored a production environment in 10 seconds and supports flexible identity table handling, company mapping, and dry-run preview modes.

title: MSDyn365BC.Sandbox.Code.History - Late Hotfix Handling
summary: The MSDyn365BC.Sandbox.Code.History repository now handles late hotfixes released by Microsoft with lower version numbers by automatically inserting them in the correct chronological position using git rebase, fixing repository bloat and confusing version order issues. Users with existing clones may need to update branches using provided automation scripts when history is rewritten.

title: Building a Plug & Play Claude Code Dev Container for AL Development
summary: Describes building a reusable dev container feature, distributed via GHCR, that installs Claude Code for AL work. Named Docker volumes keep authentication across rebuilds, and stripped git credentials stop Claude Code, running with bypassed permissions, from reaching GitHub. Next steps are AL-specific Claude configuration and moving to Anthropic's official firewall-based dev container.

title: Claude Code in a Standalone Docker Container: Building a Real Sandbox (Part 2)
summary: Stefan Maron moves his Claude Code sandbox from a VS Code dev container to a standalone docker run container, because the dev container left an IPC escape path open. The container keeps firewall, credential hardening, named volumes for auth and per-language CLAUDE.md mounts such as an AL file. Tests show local commits work and pushes are blocked. Part 3 will add AL tooling like BcContainerHelper and the AL compiler.

title: Fixing AL Language Extension Debugger on Linux with Wayland/Hyprland
summary: The AL Language Extension debugger fails on Linux with Wayland/Hyprland, showing empty Call Stack and Variables panels despite successfully connecting to Business Central. Using VS Code Dev Containers to run the AL Language Server inside an Ubuntu container while keeping the VS Code UI on Hyprland restores full debugging functionality.

title: How to Set Up a New Business Central Development Project – The 100% Correct Way
summary: This guide covers the essential setup steps for creating a new Business Central AL development project, from project creation and app.json configuration to code analysis and DevOps. It emphasizes starting with proper templates, modern naming conventions, and AL-Go for GitHub to ensure maintainability, CI/CD readiness, and AppSource compatibility.

title: Introducing ALCops — LinterCop's Next Chapter
summary: ALCops is a complete replacement for LinterCop that splits code analysis into six domain-specific analyzers (ApplicationCop, DocumentationCop, FormattingCop, LinterCop, PlatformCop, TestAutomationCop) to address structural limitations including GitHub rate limits, overgrown feature scope, and rule severity constraints. It improves code quality through better rule severity defaults, 30 code fixes, correctness fixes, and distributes via NuGet with MCP server support for AI tooling integration.

title: Introducing the “No Shortcuts” Series: The 100% Correct Way to Develop for Business Central
summary: A series introduction on best practices for Business Central AL development that prioritizes maintainability, upgrade safety, and AppSource readiness over shortcuts. It targets experienced developers seeking to reduce technical debt and build sustainable, future-proof extensions.

title: I Can Turn Off My Code. I Can't Turn Off Yours.
summary: When developers set RunTrigger to false on Insert, Modify, or DeleteAll, they silently disable all subscribers including base app code and third-party extensions. The post argues that triggers should run by default because developers cannot know at compile time what logic they would disable, and proposes the platform should dynamically check at runtime whether anything is registered on a trigger before deciding whether to skip the expensive per-row execution.

title: Optimizing BC Code History Downloads with HTTP Range Requests
summary: Optimizing the MSDyn365BC.Sandbox.Code.History repository's daily download pipeline by fixing silent failures in PowerShell scripts and implementing HTTP Range requests to reduce bandwidth usage from 800MB-2GB+ per country artifact to roughly 120MB, cutting cumulative compute time by 86% across 50 parallel countries.

title: Planning Table Indexes for the Best Performance
summary: Explains the read versus write trade-off of table indexes in Business Central: clustered and non-clustered indexes, covering indexes with IncludedFields, SIFT views and columnstore indexes. Gives rules of thumb (each index may add 10 to 20 percent write cost, keep SIFT views to one or two on write-heavy tables) and shows how to check index usage with the debugger, execution plans, RT0085 telemetry and the missing index page.

title: Swappable Claude Profiles: Per-Project Configs via Container Mounting (Part 3)
summary: Claude Code profiles enable project-specific configurations by mounting host directories as ~/.claude inside containers, allowing separate contexts, instructions, and agents for different work types. The profile system makes it practical to maintain AL development, telemetry investigation, and other specialized contexts without switching tools.

title: Turning My Coding Streams Into Blog Posts (With a Little Help From Claude)
summary: A BC developer built a Claude Code skill that turns his YouTube live coding streams into structured blog posts. It uses captions and extracted frames, then adds a pass that inserts links to official docs. He converted 26 Business Central development streams this way, which also helps the community tool CentralQ because that tool handles written content better than video.

title: You don't need the base app to run your unit tests
summary: Unit tests for self-contained Business Central logic do not require the base application to run. By structuring code as isolated sub-extensions with their own app.json files and only platform dependencies, developers can significantly reduce container startup time and pipeline costs.

title: Weekly Recap: August 7-14
summary: A weekly recap covering AL Runner v2 improvements closing emulation gaps against real BC, reference suite growth through sandbox-verified testing, bc-code-atlas enhancements for cross-app call graphs with deterministic global IDs, AL-Go fast lane hardening for multi-workflow stability, and compile-time benchmarking showing NuGet-sourced compilation is faster due to smaller dependency caches.

title: Weekly Recap: August 14-21
summary: This weekly recap covers AL Runner releases (v2.2-v2.3.1) with coverage reporting and watch mode improvements, CI/CD fixes for parallel dependency resolution and Linux builds, a major catch-up of bc-code-atlas's stale graphify-al fork that revealed hidden AL-specific behaviors and tree-sitter parser changes, and various smaller tool fixes. It highlights infrastructure improvements that prevent silent failures in builds and dependency resolution.

title: Weekly Recap: August 21-28
summary: Weekly recap covering AL Runner CI tooling fixes, Linux fast lane pipeline bugs, a major OpenPageInspection browser extension rewrite for cross-browser support, and Azure CLI authentication contributions to the navapi Business Central API client.

title: August 2025 Auckland D365 BC User Group Event
summary: A personal reflection on presenting at the Auckland D365 Business Central User Group event, highlighting the value of community engagement and sharing knowledge with peers in the BC community.

title: Avoiding UX Fragmentation When Building Business Central Extensions
summary: UX fragmentation occurs when Business Central extensions use inconsistent naming, layouts, messaging, and workflows, making the system feel disjointed to users. Developers can reduce fragmentation by establishing shared design guidelines, consistent terminology, and unified navigation across extensions.

title: BC Friday Tips #27 Replace Blank Values using Transformation Rules
summary: Transformation Rules can replace blank values in Business Central using regular expressions. Set the transformation type to "Replace" and use the pattern ^$ to match empty strings without requiring any development.

title: BC Friday Tips #28 Math Codeunit
summary: Business Central includes a built-in Math codeunit that provides constants and static methods for mathematical functions like trigonometry, logarithms, and common operations. Developers can use it to avoid duplicating mathematical logic in their code.

title: BC Friday Tips #29 Gaps in Customer Ledger Entries
summary: Customer Ledger Entries in Business Central use General Ledger Entry numbers instead of sequential numbering, which explains gaps in entry numbers and was designed historically to improve performance. Vendor Ledger Entries follow the same design pattern.

title: BC Friday Tips #30 DataAccessIntent
summary: The DataAccessIntent property can be set to ReadOnly on API pages and reports to direct the server to use a replica database, reducing load on the primary database and improving overall performance.

title: BC Friday Tips #31 Block Users using Security Group
summary: Environment-level security groups in Azure AD restrict access to Business Central instances by allowing only group members to sign in. This approach works for both production and sandbox environments.

title: BC Friday Tips #32 Unit of Measure Management Codeunit
summary: The Unit of Measure Management codeunit provides built-in functions for handling unit of measure conversions and quantity calculations in Business Central. Developers should use it instead of creating custom solutions to ensure consistency and save development time.

title: BC Friday Tips #33 Month Enum
summary: Business Central includes built-in enums for month and day-of-week recurrence patterns. Developers can reuse these existing enums rather than creating custom ones, saving development time.

title: BC Friday Tips #34 Restore Environment
summary: Business Central allows administrators to restore an environment from a previous point in time using the Admin Center, enabling recovery of accidentally deleted data from backups within the past 28 days. This feature helps protect against data loss incidents by allowing point-in-time recovery.

title: BC Friday Tips #35 Item Journal Posting and Warehouse Entries
summary: Item journal posting in AL has two codeunits: Codeunit 22 posts individual lines while Codeunit 23 posts entire batches. When warehouse entries are needed, use Codeunit 23 even for single lines, as Codeunit 22 silently fails to create warehouse entries without throwing an error.

title: BC Friday Tips #36 Emoji in BC
summary: Emojis can be displayed in Business Central to improve user experience by providing quick visual cues for statuses, warnings, and categories. They help users scan data faster and identify issues at a glance, but should be used sparingly to avoid negatively impacting the interface.

title: BC Friday Tips #37 Inherent Permissions
summary: Inherent Permissions in AL allow developers to grant temporary access during code execution without assigning permissions to individual users. This reduces permission management overhead and improves security by controlling access through code rather than user assignments.

title: BC Friday Tips #38 Keep Description
summary: The Keep Description field in General Journals prevents the Description from being cleared when users change the Account Type, which is useful for preserving descriptions in imported or auto-generated journals.

title: BC Friday Tips #39 Troubleshoot Connectivity
summary: The Troubleshooting Connectivity page helps diagnose connection issues between users' computers and Business Central by checking internet connectivity, Azure CDN resources, user authentication, and service health. Access it by appending '/connectivity' to your Business Central URL.

title: BC Friday Tips #41 Line Separator in Data Exchange Definition
summary: A hidden Line Separator field in Data Exchange Definition allows importing files with different line break formats (LF or CR) without custom development. The field is not visible through normal personalization but can be accessed via Configuration Package or code modifications.

title: BC Friday Tips #42 User Setup Management
summary: The User Setup Management codeunit provides built-in functions for checking posting dates and retrieving sales/purchase filters, helping developers avoid reinventing common logic and maintain consistency across applications.

title: BC Friday Tips #43 Regex Codeunit
summary: Business Central includes a Regex codeunit that enables pattern matching in text. It provides functions like IsMatch, Match, and Replace for validating, cleaning, and transforming text without building custom search logic.

title: BC Friday Tips #44 Changing Production Order Status
summary: When a Production Order status changes in Business Central, the system inserts a new record and deletes the old one rather than modifying it. Understanding this behavior helps avoid errors when subscribing to Insert, Modify, or Delete triggers on Production Orders.

title: BC Friday Tips #45 Hide Agents Icon
summary: Business Central now displays an Agents icon in the Role Center navigation menu. You can hide this icon by deactivating Agents in Copilot & agent capabilities settings, which helps keep the UI clean and prevents confusion for users not using AI Agents yet.

title: BC Friday Tips #46 Warning on Importing or Applying a Large Configuration Package
summary: Business Central warns when importing or applying large configuration packages because they can degrade performance and lock out users. Import warnings trigger at files over 3MB, and apply warnings trigger at packages with more than 5,000 records total.

title: BC Friday Tips #47 Enum Display Order
summary: Enum values in AL display in the order they appear in code, not by their ordinal values. This allows developers to rearrange enum values without needing to renumber ordinals.

title: BC Friday Tips #48 Save Prompt File
summary: Business Central developers can save Copilot prompts in Visual Studio Code to reuse them repeatedly or share them with team members instead of retyping.

title: BC Friday Tips #49 Page Scripting and AI
summary: Page Scripting records and replays steps in Business Central for automated testing. AI can convert these scripts into user documentation and training manuals, reducing manual writing effort.

title: BC Friday Tips #51 Dimension No. in Dimension Value
summary: The Dimension Value table contains a hidden Global Dimension No. field that reveals which shortcut dimension a dimension code belongs to, avoiding the need to check General Ledger Setup and improving lookup performance.

title: BC Friday Tips #52 Voice Chat with GitHub Copilot
summary: VS Code Speech extension enables voice chat with GitHub Copilot, allowing developers to speak prompts instead of typing, saving time and improving accessibility while coding in AL.

title: BC Friday Tips #53 Areopa Webinars
summary: Areopa hosts free webinars for Business Central consultants covering performance troubleshooting, AL development, Power Platform, AI, and test automation, led by MVPs and industry experts.

title: BC Friday Tips #54 Report Explorer
summary: The Report Explorer is a discovery tool in Business Central that helps users browse and find available reports from the Role Center or via Tell Me. It lets you locate reports by name or uncover useful ones you might not have known existed.

title: BC Friday Tips #55 CaptionClass
summary: CaptionClass is a property that creates dynamic captions changing based on data or context, with dimension fields as a common example. It helps build flexible, context-aware captions using reference codeunits from the base application.

title: BC Friday Tips #56 Understand Missing Fields in Copy Documents
summary: Some Sales Order fields do not carry over to posted shipments and invoices. For example, Shipping Agent Code and Shipping Agent Service Code exist on both Sales Header and Sales Line but only reach the Sales Shipment Header and Sales Invoice Header. As a result, copying from a posted invoice can leave fields blank, and the post recommends copying from an archived sales order instead.

title: BC Friday Tips #57 Use TestStatusOpen Procedure
summary: When adding new fields to Sales or Purchase documents in Business Central, use the TestStatusOpen procedure during validation to ensure fields cannot be edited after the document is released. This prevents accidental changes to important order data and maintains workflow consistency.

title: BC Friday Tips #58 Spotting Report with SaveValues
summary: The SaveValues property in Business Central reports remembers user-selected options on the request page. A quick way to check if SaveValues is enabled is examining the Preview button behavior: if it shows only 'Preview', SaveValues is on and keeps the request page open for adjustments; if it shows 'Preview & Close', SaveValues is off and closes the page after each run.

title: BC Friday Tips #59 Allocation Account Design
summary: Allocation Accounts automate the distribution of revenue or cost amounts through journals and documents. The feature is implemented via Codeunit 2677, which subscribes to an event before posting batch runs, intercepts journal lines, rewrites them, and posts the updated lines.

title: BC Friday Tips #60 DevToys
summary: DevToys is a free collection of utilities that support Business Central development tasks like encoding, code formatting, regex testing, and data conversion. It helps developers work more efficiently.

title: D365 Business Central: How to fix Edit in Excel Add-In Error - The service required to use this feature is turn off. Check your privacy settings.
summary: The Edit in Excel feature in Business Central may show an error message about a disabled service due to privacy settings in Excel. Users can resolve this by enabling optional connected experiences in Excel's Trust Center settings.

title: D365 Business Central: How to Fix Missing Sales Invoices in the API
summary: The Sales Invoices API in Business Central aggregates posted and unposted invoices from two source tables. When invoices are missing from the API results, running the API Data Upgrade process from the API Data Upgrade List page resolves the issue by synchronizing the underlying Sales Invoice Entity Aggregate table.

title: D365 Business Central: Why is my Job Queue Tasks Cue in Red?
summary: The Job Queue Tasks cue turns red in Business Central when more than four tasks are queued or processing. You can adjust this threshold through the Cue Setup page or directly in the Cue Setup table using a configuration package.

title: How to Write a Good Success Message
summary: Success messages confirm user actions in Business Central by reassuring users that tasks like posting invoices or importing orders were completed. Well-designed success messages build trust, boost confidence, and create a professional experience while preventing users from doubting their actions.

title: How to Write Error Messages That Help
summary: Error messages significantly impact user experience in enterprise software. The post explains how to write clear, actionable error messages that guide users to solutions rather than leaving them frustrated, with practical examples showing vague messages transformed into helpful ones.

title: Introducing BC Prompt Kit: How I Started My AI Journey
summary: BC Prompt Kit is a collection of organized prompts for developers to adopt AI in Business Central and AL development. It covers base development, feature analysis, documentation, and refactoring, designed to help developers overcome initial skepticism and integrate AI into their daily workflow.

title: Progress Dialog: Making Business Central Responsive
summary: Progress Dialog provides user feedback during long-running ERP tasks in Business Central, reducing uncertainty and duplicate actions. This post explains when to use Progress Dialog, shows AL code examples, and provides seven best practices for writing clear, confidence-building progress messages.

title: BC Friday Tips #61 Check AppSource App Update History
summary: When evaluating AppSource apps for Business Central, check the last updated date before installing. Apps without recent updates risk containing bugs or failing to use current AL features since the platform changes with each release.

title: BC Friday Tips #62 VS Code AL Themes
summary: The AL Language extension in VS Code includes built-in themes called Business Central Light and Business Central Dark available since version 16.00 to improve code readability and reduce eye strain.

title: BC Friday Tips #63 Sharing Full Screenshot
summary: Sharing full screenshots in Business Central troubleshooting and communication provides more context about company, user, and environment, making issues easier to reproduce and reducing follow-up questions.

title: BC Friday Tips #64 Filter Tokens Codeunit
summary: The Filter Tokens codeunit enables converting text input into date filters with shortcuts like T for Today, matching FlowFilter behavior for consistent user experience in extensions.

title: BC Friday Tips #65 Freeze Column Property
summary: The FreezeColumn property keeps selected columns visible when users scroll horizontally through list pages with many fields, reducing the need for horizontal scrolling and keeping important data in view.

title: BC Friday Tips #66 API v2 app
summary: The Exclude_APIV2 app is a hidden Microsoft extension in Business Central that contains standard API V2 objects. Developers can explore this app via symbol files in VS Code to understand Microsoft's API design patterns and reference it when building or extending their own APIs.

title: BC Friday Tips #67 Reset Page Number in RDLC
summary: The ResetPageNumber property in RDLC reports restarts page numbering at 1 for each group or document, matching user expectations when printing multiple groups.

title: BC Friday Tips #68 Always Use Field Validation
summary: Field validation in Business Central extensions ensures all business logic runs and prevents data corruption when other apps subscribe to validation events. Bypassing validation can create hidden bugs by skipping trigger logic even when fields appear correct.

title: BC Friday Tips #69 Item Blocked Fields
summary: The Item table in Business Central has multiple blocked fields (Blocked, Sales Blocked, Purchasing Blocked, Service Blocked) that control item restrictions. Checking only the main Blocked field can miss module-specific restrictions and cause logic errors.

title: BC Friday Tips #70 Email Scenario Attachment
summary: Email scenarios in Business Central can include default attachments that are automatically sent with every email, such as terms and conditions attached to invoice emails. This prevents missed attachments and ensures consistent communication without requiring manual user action each time.

title: BC Friday Tips #71 BlankZero Property
summary: The BlankZero property on numeric fields can be set to true to display empty values instead of zero, reducing visual clutter and helping users focus on meaningful data in optional fields.

title: BC Friday Tips #72 Inlay Hints
summary: Inlay Hints in VS Code display inline parameter names and return types while coding in AL, helping developers understand function signatures without hovering or jumping to definitions. This feature is particularly useful for procedures with many parameters and can be configured to appear on demand to keep the editor clean.

title: BC Friday Tips #73 Show All Configuration Package Errors
summary: When applying a Configuration Package in Business Central, users can view all errors on a single page by clicking the Error section, allowing faster review and resolution without checking entries individually.

title: BC Friday Tips #74 Copy Document and Custom Field
summary: When adding custom fields to Sales Header or Sales Invoice Header tables, developers must consider how the Copy Document feature will handle those fields. The post explains that custom fields are automatically copied along with documents, requiring developers to decide whether values should be copied, cleared, or recalculated to maintain data integrity.

title: BC Friday Tips #75 Dynamics BC Excel Reports
summary: Excel Reports objects in Business Central belong to the Dynamics BC Excel Reports extension rather than the Base Application, requiring developers to add it as a dependency when extending these objects.

title: BC Friday Tips #76 Barcode Fonts in RDL Reports
summary: Creating barcodes in Business Central SaaS reports requires setting the FontFamily property directly in RDL files without installing fonts locally. This approach works out of the box and supports various barcode types like Code 93 using fonts such as IDAutomationC93M.

title: BC Friday Tips #77 TestField Show Record Action
summary: TestField automatically adds a Show Record button to error dialogs when field validation fails, letting users jump directly to the problem record. This feature works natively for tables with single primary keys like Customer, but not for compound primary key tables like Sales Header.

title: BC Friday Tips #78 InitValue Property
summary: The InitValue property sets a default value for new table fields when records are created, initialized, or cleared. This property applies only to new records and cannot be used on standard fields through table extensions.

title: BC Friday Tips #79 Change Log Deletion on One Field
summary: Enabling deletion logging on a single primary key field is sufficient to track who deleted a record in Business Central, avoiding unnecessary duplicate Change Log entries. This approach keeps the change log smaller and easier to review.

title: BC Friday Tips #80 Business Central Trivia
summary: Business Central Trivia is a website where users can test their BC knowledge, earn points, and compete on a leaderboard. It provides an engaging alternative to traditional training materials for consultants, developers, and power users.

title: BC Friday Tips #81 Keep BCContainerHelper Up to Date
summary: BCContainerHelper is a PowerShell module for Business Central container workflows. Keeping it updated ensures you get the latest bug fixes and performance improvements that may resolve container issues.

title: BC Friday Tips #82 Excel Buffer Character Limit
summary: Excel Buffer in Business Central has a 250-character limit on field values. When longer text is written to it, Business Central throws an error instead of silently truncating, which can cause Excel exports to fail.

title: BC Friday Tips #83 Check Whether a Record Has Changed
summary: The Record.IsDirty() method detects whether a record has been modified without requiring manual tracking. This pattern simplifies code when applying multiple field updates to a record.

title: Change Behaviour on VAT Prod. Posting Group - Prices Incl. VAT in v28.2
summary: Business Central v28.2 changed how it handles VAT Product Posting Group changes on G/L Account purchase lines when Prices Incl. VAT is enabled. Previously the total including VAT remained constant, but now the unit cost recalculates and the total amount decreases.

title: SymLynx
summary: SymLynx is a VS Code extension that solves the problem of duplicating configuration files across multiple Business Central repositories by using symbolic links to point to a single master copy, eliminating file synchronization issues and config drift.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Month End Accruals for GRNI Purchase Orders and Unposted Purchase Invoices
summary: This post explains how to identify and accrue for unposted purchase invoices and goods received not invoiced (GRNI) purchase orders at month end using the Purchase Lines page in Analysis Mode, then post accruals through a Recurring General Journal.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Three ways to post Sales Ledger Cash Receipts in Business Central
summary: This post explains three methods for posting customer cash receipts in Business Central: using the Cash Receipt Journal, the Register Customer Payments feature, and posting cash directly through the Bank Reconciliation process. Each method suits different workflows and experience levels, with the bank reconciliation approach offering efficiency by combining cash posting with bank statement reconciliation.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – How to post a Sales Credit for an Item without affecting Inventory using an Item Charge
summary: When issuing a sales credit for an item that remains with the customer, using an Item Charge linked to the original sales shipment is preferable to posting directly to a GL account because it creates value entries that correctly update inventory reports and the Sales Amount (Actual) on item ledger entries.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Error Message “You have one or more documents that must be posted before you post document no….” when posting a Journal
summary: When posting a journal in Business Central, an error occurs if the journal's number series has manual numbers disabled but the user tries to enter a custom document number. The post explains three solutions: enable manual numbers on the number series, remove the number series from the batch, or use the renumber function to auto-generate the next sequential number.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central Migration Post – Part 1: What do my migrated Opening Balances look like in Business Central
summary: When migrating from Dynamics GP to Business Central, opening balances for customers, vendors, and general ledger accounts are transferred via Microsoft's migration tool. Customer and vendor unapplied transactions appear as ledger entries, while GL balances migrate as summarized monthly amounts with the main segment becoming the GL code and other segments converted to dimensions.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – What does my migrated GP Historical Data look like in Business Central
summary: After a Dynamics GP to Business Central migration, historical transactions are stored in special tables rather than as ledger entries. Sales and receivables history, including applied payments, is shown through factbox tiles on the Customer List, and vendor history works the same way. Financial journal history is reached from the Chart of Accounts through the GP Detail Snapshot action.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – How to default a General Ledger account onto a Purchase Invoice using “Recurring Purchase Lines”
summary: Recurring Purchase Lines automatically default General Ledger accounts and other details onto purchase invoices when a vendor is selected, streamlining repetitive invoice entry such as monthly rent payments.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Why when I create new users do they get full access by default
summary: New users in Business Central automatically receive full access to their first company based on their assigned license. Administrators can prevent this by modifying permission sets in the License Configuration page.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Handling the message “Only the Posting No. Series can be filled in on recurring journals” in Recurring Journals
summary: Business Central blocks a regular No. Series on Recurring General Journal batches; the author assumes this is because lines stay after posting, so numbers would repeat. Two workarounds are shown: set a Posting No. Series on the batch so posted entries get unique numbers, or put date placeholders in the Document No. field so each posting builds a unique number from the posting date.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Why isn’t Payment Tolerance being taken automatically in the Cash Receipt Journal?
summary: Payment Tolerance in Business Central can automatically write off small remaining invoice balances when a payment is applied. The post shows that tolerance is only taken when the Cash Receipt Journal line has Document Type set to Payment; otherwise no tolerance warning appears and no tolerance GL entry posts.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – How to proportionally split costs across Dimensions using Statistical Accounts and Allocation Accounts
summary: This post explains how to automatically split costs across cost center dimensions in Business Central using Statistical Accounts and Allocation Accounts. It demonstrates a scenario where heating expenses are distributed proportionally to departments based on square footage, streamlining accurate cost allocation without manual intervention.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – Some Considerations when Changing Standard Cost on an Item Card
summary: Changing standard cost directly on an item card in Business Central has two critical side effects: stock keeping units are not automatically updated, and existing inventory is not revalued. Understanding these considerations is essential before making cost changes to avoid unexpected cost adjustments during sales transactions.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – How to use the “Recurring Requisition Worksheet” for Recurring Purchase Orders
summary: The Recurring Requisition Worksheet automates repeated purchases of the same items by preserving worksheet lines after creating purchase orders and automatically updating order dates. This feature saves time for businesses that place regular orders for specific items or services.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – How to Recreate the GL Summary Enquiry using G/L Account Balance, Analysis Mode or an Analysis View
summary: When migrating from Dynamics GP to Business Central, GL account structures change from segmented codes to single codes with dimensions. The post explains three methods to recreate Dynamics GP's GL Summary Enquiry view in Business Central: filtering the Chart of Accounts page, using Analysis Mode with natural language in Copilot, or creating an Analysis View.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – How to easily convert your GP word templates to BC word layouts
summary: Converting Dynamics GP Word templates to Business Central Word layouts can be done efficiently by removing GP content controls, importing into Business Central's Report Layouts, updating and exporting to add BC data, then editing in Word to add BC fields. This approach helps during migration by preserving the original design without full recreation.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – How to Control your General Ledger Code and Dimension Combinations using Allowed Values Filter
summary: When migrating from Dynamics GP to Business Central, General Ledger segments become dimensions that are available to any account by default. The post explains how to control which dimension values can be used with specific GL accounts using the Allowed Values Filter feature to replicate Dynamics GP's segment-code restrictions.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – A Closer look at the Free “Internal Administrator” and “Dynamics 365 Administrator” Licences
summary: Business Central offers free administrative licenses to Microsoft 365 tenant administrators who perform setup and security tasks. The Internal Administrator and Dynamics 365 Administrator licenses are automatically assigned to Global Administrators and Dynamics 365 Administrators respectively, giving them limited administrative capabilities without purchasing paid licenses.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central – How to change the VAT amount on a Purchase Invoice or Purchase Order
summary: Adjusting VAT amounts on purchase invoices and orders when Business Central's calculations differ from supplier invoices requires configuring the maximum allowed VAT difference and enabling the allow VAT difference option in setup pages, then editing VAT via the statistics view.

title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – The Arrival of Smartlist Features via “Add Fields from Related Tables in Analysis Mode”
summary: Business Central introduced 'Add fields from related tables in Analysis mode', a feature that mirrors Dynamics GP's Smartlist tool, enabling users to create custom reports by combining columns from related tables directly within list pages and analysis views without third-party tools.

summary: Copilot Agent works at a task level across multiple AL objects and files, unlike Chat or Edit which work on single selections. It works best when used as a guided collaborator with explicit constraints, clear scope, and incremental steps rather than as an autonomous solution builder.

title: API Pages vs API Queries in Business Central: When to Use Each
summary: API pages and API queries are two distinct REST API object types in Business Central with different purposes. API pages support full CRUD operations and are best for write operations, while API queries are optimized for read-only access with multi-table joins and server-side aggregation. Understanding when to use each type is critical for performance and integration design.

title: Quick Tip: CalcFields vs SetAutoCalcFields in AL
summary: FlowFields in Business Central are not stored in the database and must be calculated explicitly. title: Quick Tip: Almost Every BC Major Release Gets Paused. Are Your Environments Ready?
summary: Business Central major release rollouts get paused frequently due to discovered issues, and this is normal process design since 2020. Environments already upgraded before a pause cannot be rolled back, but those not yet upgraded get rescheduled safely. Partners should schedule production updates late in the window, configure notification recipients, and test in sandboxes to manage the risk effectively.

title: Quick Tip: How Can You Download the Standard Business Central Power BI Reports?

title: Quick Tip: Troubleshooting Business Central Power BI Reports: My 5-Minute Checklist
summary: Most Business Central Power BI issues stem from configuration problems rather than Power BI itself. title: Quick Tip: Runtime Version and Business Central Version Are Not the Same Thing
summary: Explains that Business Central has three different version numbers: the platform/internal build, the release wave name and the app.json runtime version. Only the runtime version decides which AL features compile, and it sets the minimum platform an extension can be published to. title: Quick Tip: It’s Time to Move to the Word Add-in Data Picker
summary: A community forum user reports that since August 2026, fields newly inserted through the classic XML Mapping pane in Word report layouts show placeholder text instead of data, while older mapped fields keep working; the cause appears to sit in Word rather than Business Central. The release includes substantial improvements across Copilot and agents, AL development, reporting and analytics, financial management, supply chain, electronic documents, and sustainability, with dedicated What's New sessions organized by topic area.

title: Business Central Data Mirroring to Microsoft Fabric Is Coming
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 introduces data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric, a new analytical data path that synchronizes selected tables and companies to Fabric's OneLake for analytics consumption. This simplifies analytics architecture by eliminating the need to repeatedly extract transactional data through APIs, making it easier to build enterprise data platforms combining Business Central with other sources.

title: Business Central 29: Introducing Composite Document Layouts
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 introduces Composite Document Layouts, a modular approach to Word document layouts that separates body content, visual theming, and headers/footers into reusable components combined at runtime rather than maintaining separate complete layouts for each combination.

title: Copilot is just a fancy autocomplete (vol.2)
summary: The author says GitHub Copilot Agent mode in VS Code has replaced Edits in her own AL development work. She recommends turning on the Todo List Tool, raising Max Requests, and adding copilot-instructions.md with a project overview. She also names her preferred models (Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-5, Grok Code Fast 1) and MCP servers for AL, and warns that too many tools use up the context window.

title: Format Cheatsheet
summary: A reference guide showing how the Format() function outputs different data types (DateTime, Date, Time, Guid, Decimal, Boolean, Option, Enum, Duration, RecordId, DateFormula) across nine format options (0-7 and 9), helping developers quickly find the correct format specification for their needs.

title: Distributing Agents with Plugins
summary: Distribution of custom agents to teams is accomplished through plugins, which package agents, skills, and MCP configurations in a shared repository that team members can install with one click in GitHub Copilot or Claude Code. The post explains how to set up marketplace and plugin manifests to enable seamless sharing across ecosystems without manual file copying.

title: Claude Code: Tiny Tips
summary: Summary withheld: an Opus review found that the machine-written summary did not match the post. Read the original post.

title: Copilot is just a fancy autocomplete (vol.3) - Steps towards agentic development
summary: This post explains five progressive steps toward agentic development: custom agents tailored to specific workflows, skills for reusable task sequences, reflection loops to improve agent instructions, sub-agents for parallel research with isolated context windows, and background agents running in terminals or pipelines without direct supervision.

title: Copilot is agent-first, Claude Code is skill-first
summary: Summary withheld: an Opus review found that the machine-written summary did not match the post. Read the original post.

title: Context is a voting chamber
summary: Summary withheld: an Opus review found that the machine-written summary did not match the post. Read the original post.

title: ALCops: The Next Chapter of LinterCop
summary: ALCops is a new community-driven code analyzer collection for AL that succeeds LinterCop, with about 95% of the original rules migrated. It provides VS Code extension and AL-Go support for daily AL development, with future work on Azure DevOps integration and AI tool compatibility.

title: ALCops: The Story So Far
summary: ALCops is a community-driven collection of code analyzers for AL that reached v1.0 after six months of development with over 480 merged pull requests. It provides focused specialized analyzers for language correctness, code smells, formatting, documentation, and testing, now integrated with AI assistants through an MCP server and replacing the earlier LinterCop project by October 2026.

title: Rethinking LinterCop: Preparing for the Next Chapter
summary: LinterCop, a code analyzer for AL, faces architectural limitations that require fundamental redesign. The post explains tight coupling with the AL language, distribution challenges through GitHub, scope creep as a "Swiss Army Knife," and DevOps integration issues, leading to a proposed LinterCop 2.0 rebuild.

title: Directions EMEA 2025
summary: A conference attendee reflects on Directions EMEA 2025, highlighting agentic AI as the central theme and covering practical insights from development sessions on topics like GitHub versus Azure DevOps, building knowledge-first AI workflows, and implementing AI agents in Business Central. The post emphasizes how AI tools have become practical and applicable to daily development work beyond just coding.

title: Dutch Dynamics Community Event 18 november 2025
summary: Recap of a Dutch Dynamics Community evening in November 2025, covering two of the five parallel sessions. One showed a document management approach that links Dynamics 365 Sales and SharePoint through Dataverse metadata and PnP Modern Search. The other covered connecting Business Central to Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Warehouse Only Mode for advanced warehousing; no dual-rights license exists yet, and the setup can be a step towards Finance and Operations.

title: Dutch Dynamics Community Event 10 February 2026
summary: A Dutch Dynamics Community event on February 10, 2026 featured technical sessions on creating AI agents inside Business Central (released in version 27.4) and using Copilot for AI pair programming in AL development. The post emphasizes how agents work within the existing Business Central environment and the importance of effective prompts for better AI assistance.

title: Troubleshooting Series – Ep2 – Admin Center – Sessions
summary: The Sessions window in the Business Central Admin Center allows partners and delegated admins to view active sessions across all server instances and cancel problematic ones to improve system performance and resolve resource issues.

title: Handling Business Central Telemetry like a boss: iFacto Telemetry – Pt. 3
summary: The iFacto Telemetry app extends Business Central's built-in telemetry capabilities by adding custom events to track missing indexes, function performance, media orphans, installed apps, delegated user actions, feature management status, and retention policies. It helps administrators monitor system health and performance across multiple customers and environments.

title: Obsoleted and “no longer invoked” events in v26 Business Central
summary: Business Central v26 removed invocation of 82 obsoleted events from the legacy invoice posting system while keeping them in the codebase for backward compatibility. Code subscribing to these non-invoked events will compile and publish but fail silently at runtime, creating a hidden risk for developers upgrading from earlier versions.

title: BCTalent – Escape Rooms
summary: For a Red Carpet event in Microsoft's BCTalent program, the author and AJ built a proof-of-concept Business Central app that runs escape rooms. Consultant and developer venues contain rooms that unlock as trainees complete tasks inside BC. Tasks are checked automatically through event subscribers and test codeunits, progress is logged with telemetry, and the author hopes the framework will later reach ISVs and events.

title: Troubleshooting Series – Ep3 – Missing Indexes
summary: Troubleshooting missing indexes in Business Central SaaS environments requires understanding the Missing Indexes page, which reflects SQL DMV data that resets after server restart. Since developers can only add indexes through apps, careful analysis using telemetry to track missing indexes over time helps identify which indexes are truly necessary before implementation.

title: Troubleshooting Series – Ep4 – Event Recorder
summary: The Event Recorder is a Business Central troubleshooting tool that captures all events during a specific process by starting and stopping recording. It helps developers and troubleshooters identify performance issues, validate functional behavior, debug customizations, understand extension behavior, and document system processes.

title: Analyzing BC Telemetry with AI with the “BC Telemetry Buddy”
summary: BC Telemetry Buddy is a VSCode extension and Model Context Protocol tool that lets users query Business Central telemetry data through natural conversation using GitHub Copilot, without needing to write KQL or have separate subscriptions. It includes features for event discovery, stack trace analysis, report generation, and custom chat modes for focused analysis workflows.

title: BC Telemetry Buddy – 84 commits later..
summary: BC Telemetry Buddy evolved from a proof of concept to a production-ready tool for analyzing Business Central telemetry. The v1.0.0 release transformed it from a bundled extension into modular components, added AI-powered chat features for data discovery and analysis, and implemented comprehensive testing and CI/CD pipelines.

title: BC Telemetry Buddy  – When Your 12-Year-Old Accidentally Helps You Find a Problem
summary: BC Telemetry Buddy is an MCP-based VS Code tool that lets you question Business Central telemetry in natural language instead of writing KQL. A casual demo question exposed a customer whose background queue codeunit ran slow full table scans on an unindexed queue table that lacked a retention policy. Diagnosis took about 15 minutes, and enabling retention plus adding an index removed the waste.

title: Escape Room App gone public!
summary: The BCTalent Escape Room framework, a tool for building interactive learning experiences in Business Central, has been released as open source. It provides a documented platform for creating custom rooms and puzzles for training, onboarding, and feature adoption rather than complete puzzle content.

title: Troubleshooting Series – Ep5 – Telemetry
summary: Telemetry is essential for troubleshooting Business Central SaaS because it provides evidence about when issues occur, their frequency, affected customers, and performance metrics without SQL access or profilers. The post covers two telemetry channels (environment-level and app/extension-level), Microsoft-provided tools like Power BI apps and Azure Data Explorer, and the BC Telemetry Buddy tool that makes querying telemetry easier through AI assistance.

title: I built the tool .. but forgot the skill..
summary: Building effective AI tools for telemetry analysis requires more than access to data and dashboards. The quality of questions asked and critical evaluation of AI responses are the real limiting factors in diagnosing performance issues.

title: BC Telemetry Buddy .. now with (community) knowledge
summary: BC Telemetry Buddy now includes a two-layer knowledge base that shares telemetry troubleshooting patterns and investigation playbooks across the community. The tool stores both shared community knowledge and local customer-specific insights as markdown files, allowing the AI to start problem-solving with context rather than from scratch.

title: OptimAL – performance still matters
summary: OptimAL is a structured Microsoft performance initiative for BC partners and ISVs that combines maturity assessment, skills training, telemetry analysis, and hands-on code optimization. The program addresses how most BC performance issues stem from partner code rather than the platform, with participants achieving dramatic improvements like reducing batch job runtime from 5+ hours to under 20 minutes or improving page load times by 93%.

title: “the waldo way”
summary: A CTO reflects on building a pre-packaged agentic development harness for the team to accelerate adoption, but questions whether removing setup friction also eliminates valuable learning opportunities. The post explores the tradeoff between speed-and-consistency versus developer ownership and skill-building.

title: Business Central data in Fabric: the way it should be
summary: Business Central now supports native data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric, allowing users to replicate their tables as Delta Parquet files in OneLake with SQL query access. The feature enters public preview in release wave 2 (likely version 29.1) and requires only workspace setup and table selection with no impact on BC performance or API limits.

title: The Business Central 2026 release wave 2 docs nobody asked for ..
summary: Waldo created an interactive navigation tool for the Business Central 2026 Wave 2 release event videos, mapping 319 features across 38 videos with direct timestamps to help users find specific announcements without watching all 7+ hours. The site uses AI to extract features and quotes from auto-captions and cross-references them with official documentation to highlight gaps or conflicts.

title: What's New: Sales Lines Suggestions with Copilot (2024 release wave 1)
summary: Sales line suggestions with Copilot in Business Central, as covered in the 2024 release wave 1 What's New video. Covers better keyword extraction and context understanding, faster product search, blanket order linking, document-specific search, units of measure, and CSV upload with column mapping and caching.

title: What's New: Demo Data for Analytics (2025 release wave 2)
summary: Business Central 2025 release wave 2 adds an optional 'analytics' package to the Contoso demo data tool, with more sales and purchasing documents and more variation for reporting and Power BI demos. It can be installed from the tool or is included when all demo data is chosen for a new company.

title: Upgrade Business Central Sandbox to Preview Version
summary: Updating an existing Business Central sandbox to a preview version from the admin center, so upcoming functionality can be tested with real customer data, configurations and extensions. Covers scheduling the update, post-upgrade testing and preview limitations, including deletion 30 days after GA.

title: What's New: User Experience Enhancements (2025 release wave 2)
summary: Business Central 2025 release wave 2 user experience changes: factbox resizing, Advanced Tellme semantic search (preview), extra instructions for the sales order agent, week numbers in date pickers, and a data masking property for sensitive fields (preview).

title: Business Central Launch Event 2025 Release Wave 1 - Recording of Live Opening
summary: Business Central 2025 release wave 1 launch event opening: the sales order agent is in public preview in more countries, agent billing is by consumption messages (private preview), and the payables agent is shown in private preview with a public preview planned later this year. Also covers Copilot autofill and summarize, sustainability, e-documents, manufacturing, Power BI and Excel reports, admin features (flexible update management, unified extensions view, tenant discovery endpoint, customer-managed keys), developer tooling and posting performance improvements.

title: Introducing: PTEs in Admin Center (2025 release wave 1)
summary: PTEs in the Business Central admin center (2025 release wave 1): the admin center now lists PTEs and dev extensions next to global apps, lets admins uninstall apps and see dependencies, and exposes the same data in admin center API version 2.25.

title: Work Seamlessly with Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Teams
summary: Business Central used with Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Excel and Word in a scripted customer-service and sales scenario. It shows Teams chat links and tabs, read-only access via a Microsoft 365 account, a Power Automate escalation, Outlook contact insights and quotes, and Excel/Word editing.

title: Introducing: Sustainability in Business Central (2024 release wave 1)
summary: Sustainability in Business Central (2024 release wave 1) covers the foundational module for recording and reporting greenhouse gas emissions: setup, chart of sustainability accounts, journals, ledger entries, three standard reports and demo data. Regulatory reports and APIs are not part of this wave.

title: Concurrency in Business Central: Parallel processes without deadlocks and timeouts
summary: Business Central concurrency session covering SQL Server lock types, isolation levels, lock escalation at about 5,000 locks, and deadlocks, with demos of loops, chunking, SEMAPHORE locks, number sequences and auto increment in a cinema booking case. Lock timeout defaults are 10 seconds on-premise and 35 seconds in SaaS.

title: What's New: Business Central Integration with Dataverse (2024 release wave 1)
summary: Business Central integration with Dataverse in 2024 release wave 1: data sync changes (linked environments, table and field mappings on existing integration tables, troubleshooting fact box), synthetic relationships, multi-company virtual tables with mapping plugins, and business event monitoring with Application Insights.

title: Introducing Payment Times Analysis in Business Central (2023 release wave 2)
summary: Payment Times Analysis in Business Central (2023 release wave 2) analyzes whether vendor and customer payments happen on or after due dates. It can aggregate by company size or by custom period, and the video demos both, including drill-down, history and printing.

title: Transfer Environments
summary: Transferring Business Central environments between Microsoft Entra tenants through the tenant admin center: how to start a transfer in the source tenant, cancel pending ones, accept in the destination tenant, and the requirements (permissions, license, quota, timing limits).

title: Business Central 29: New ModuleInfo Properties Explained
summary: ModuleInfo in Business Central 29 (Runtime 18.0 or later) gets four new properties: help, ULA, privacy statement and context sensitive help URL. They expose app manifest metadata to AL code. The video demos reading them with NavApp.GetCurrentModuleInfo and NavApp.GetModuleInfo, and compares this with version 28.

title: Introducing: Composite Document Layouts (2026 release wave 2)
summary: Composite document layouts in Business Central (2026 release wave 2) split a report layout into a body layout (structure), a theme (colors, fonts, branding) and a header-footer layout, and apply the theme and header-footer at runtime. Covers layered defaults (global, company, report, layout), custom themes from the UI or AL, the themes and header-footer layouts Microsoft plans to ship, and rollout through feature management and layout status.

title: What's New: Migrate Record Links and Notes (2025 release wave 2)
summary: Migrating record links and notes from an on-premises database to Business Central online as part of cloud migration (2025 release wave 2). Covers the buffer table, the Migrate record links and notes action on the cloud migration management page, the warnings field, and the required order: replication, then migration, then user mapping.

title: Business Central Under the Hood episode 4: How we built Copilot Chat in Business Central
summary: Copilot Chat in Business Central: how Microsoft built it, covering architecture, intent condensation, data grounding, meta prompts, jailbreak prevention, and test-driven prompt engineering. Copilot Chat is in public preview and available only in US environments, per the video.

title: What's new in E-Documents: Overview (2026 release wave 2)
summary: Overview of EDI in Business Central's e-documents framework (2026 release wave 2): purchase order, sales order, order response and remittance advice exchange in XML, with a demo and three new French e-reporting formats. Feature status is not stated in the video.

title: Microsoft Sizzle: Business Central Agents In Action
summary: A short (about 98 seconds) Microsoft sizzle video about the Business Central Sales Order Agent and Payables Agent. It describes what each agent automates and says users can start building their own custom agents today. It is a high-level marketing overview, not a how-to.

title: What's New: Analyze Performance Issues with Scheduled Profiles (2024 release wave 2)
summary: Scheduled profiles in Business Central (2024 release wave 2) capture performance profiles automatically in the background based on rules, including for web service calls. The video demos setting up a profile schedule and analyzing the captured results, and contrasts this with the interactive in-client profiler.

title: What's New: Enhanced MCP Server (2026 release wave 1)
summary: Business Central MCP server enhancements in 2026 release wave 1: configuration validation, import/export, connection string setup, telemetry and auditing, MCP resources and embedded resources. Support for MCP hosts other than Copilot Studio, such as VS Code, is in public preview.

title: What's New: Reservation Worksheet and Fulfillment Suggestions (2023 release wave 2)
summary: Reservation Worksheet and the Reserved from Stock indicator in Business Central (2023 release wave 2): how to see reservation status on demand documents, allocate stock with allocation policies, and push fully reserved documents to warehouse shipments, inventory picks and consumption journals.

title: 20260126 - Excel Report Layouts: From Basics to Refreshable, Real-Time Reporting
summary: Excel report layouts in Business Central: a four-step process (get workbook with data contract, lay out data, import, test) and refreshable reports that use OData, Power Query and APIs. Covers data contract rules, hidden metadata sheets, OneDrive setup, permissions and password limits.

title: Sales Order Agent - Working with a Personal or Shared Folder (2026)
summary: Sales order agent in Business Central can be pointed at a specific Outlook folder instead of the inbox, which lets you test with a personal account and only selected emails.
